WMT.rationale: Walmart is a fundamentally sound franchise with accelerating earnings (+19.6% YoY EPS growth on +7.3% revenue), stable gross margins (25.1%), and a durable competitive position (11% U.S. retail share, 15 consecutive quarters of 10%+ e-commerce growth). However, the stock is not cheap: at ~40x PE with a 5% earnings earnings yield,,,,, 0% below the 10Y Treasury yield, the market is pricing in continued high-teens earnings growth at a multiple that leaves no margin of safety for a 3% net-margin retailer. The PE has de-rated ~25% from its 53x peak, but remains historically rich. Operating cash flow declined 12.4% YoY in Q1, weakening the quality-of-earnings argument. The Cleveland Research comp-sales warning (2026-07-01) and management's below-consensus FY2027 guidance ($2.75–$2.85 vs. $2.91 consensus) signal near-term execution risk. The August 20 earnings report is a potential catalyst but could go either way — it is not a clear positive re-rating event. Net: excellent franchise, fair-to-slightly-rich valuation, no compelling near-term catalyst to drive upside. Score sits near neutral.
key_factors: YoY EPS diluted +19.6% (Q1 FY2027: $0.67 vs $0.56 prior year) on +7.3% YoY revenue growth ($177.75B vs $165.61B)
Gross margin expanded to 25.1% from 24.9% YoY; net margin improved to 3.2% from 2.8% YoY
Operating cash flow declined -12.4% YoY ($4.74B vs $5.41B) and -47.9% QoQ vs Q3, weakening earnings quality
PE diluted at 39.77x, near the floor of its 365-day range (37.6x–55.4x), representing ~25% de-rating from ~53x peak
Earnings yield of 2.5% sits 207bp below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, creating a negative spread that pressures the multiple
Walmart Connect advertising grew 46% to ~$6.4B in FY2026 and 37% in Q1 FY2027, providing high-margin profit optionality
Walmart captured 11.08% of U.S. retail sales in 2025, crossing 10% threshold for first time
Management maintained FY2027 EPS guidance at $2.75–$2.85, below Wall Street consensus of $2.91
Cleveland Research (2026-07-01) flagged deceleration in U.S. comparable store sales, triggering 4.98% stock decline
Next earnings report August 20, 2026 (est. Q2 EPS ~$0.74–$0.75) — potential catalyst but directionally uncertain
Liabilities-to-equity of 1.88x is moderate but stable; ROE of 23% is healthy
PEG ratio of 4.24 vs industry 1.92 indicates the stock prices in significant growth expectations
